summary: Julius Dutoit (1872–1958) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Munich, Giessen, and Erlangen-Nuremberg (PhD), learning under Adalbert Kuhn and Ernst Kuhn. He later served as director of the Riemenschneider-Gymnasium from 1929 to 1934.

Julius Eggeling (1842–1918) was an Indologist who studied at Breslau and Berlin under Stenzler, Weber, Böhtlingk, and Aufrecht. He served as secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society, taught Sanskrit at UCL, and was professor at Edinburgh (1875–1914).

Julius Euting (1839–1913) was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and Ernst Heinrich Meier, later serving as director at the Bibliothèque nationale et universitaire and honorary professor at Strasbourg.
Julius Evola (1898–1974) was a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at ITI L. Da Vinci and Sapienza University of Rome, and held a post at the Ahnenerbe from 1943 to 1945.

Julius Grill (1840–1930) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Heidelberg, Tübingen (PhD under Rudolf von Roth), and Jena. He taught at Maulbronn and Blaubeuren before serving as professor of Old Testament exegesis at Tübingen (1888–1913).

Julius Jolly (1849–1932) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Munich, Berlin, and Leipzig under Martin Haug, Albrecht Weber, and Hermann Brockhaus. He was Tagore professor at Calcutta (1882–1883) and a professor at Würzburg (1877–1920).

Julius Jüthner (1866–1945) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the German University of Prague and held academic posts at the University of Fribourg (circa 1898–1903) and the University of Innsbruck (circa 1903–1937).

Julius Klaproth (1783–1835) was a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg and held a chair at the University of Bonn from circa 1816 to 1835.
Julius Laber (1884–1944) was an Indology scholar. He studied at the universities of Berlin, Freiburg, Leipzig, and Bonn, completing his PhD at Bonn and studying under Hermann Jacobi in 1908.

Julius Leumann was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Geneva, Zurich, Leipzig, and Strasbourg (PhD), learning under Ernst Leumann, Heinrich Hübschmann, and others. He served as teacher and later rector at Kantonsschule Frauenfeld (1906–1928).

Julius Lipner (born 1946) specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Jnana-Deepa Vidyapeeth, Jadavpur, and King's College London under H. D. Lewis. He taught at Birmingham before becoming Professor of Hinduism at Cambridge (1975–2013).

Julius Mohl (1800–1876) worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and Sinological studies. He studied at Tübingen and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy, Abel-Rémusat, and Burnouf, later serving as professor at Tübingen and professor of Persian at Collège de France (1847–1876).

Julius Müller (1801–1878) worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Breslau, Göttingen, and Berlin, and held professorial posts at the universities of Göttingen (~1831–1835), Marburg (~1835–1839), and Halle-Wittenberg (~1839–1878).

Julius Pokorny (1887–1970) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Vienna under Paul Kretschmer and Rudolf Much. He held posts at Berlin as professor of Celtology (1920–1935), Bern, Zurich, Fribourg, Munich, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Kiel.

Julius Schubring (1839–1914) pursued academic studies at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (circa 1857–1858), the University of Bonn (circa 1858–1860), and the University of Göttingen (circa 1860–1862).

Julius Schwab (1852–1928) was an Indologist. He studied under Martin Haug and Ernst Kuhn, earning his PhD from the University of Munich. He held library posts at the Badische Landesbibliothek (1882) and the Freiburg University Library (1887).

Julius Wellhausen (1844–1918) was a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald, and held academic posts at Greifswald, Halle-Wittenberg, Marburg, and Göttingen (circa 1892–1913).

Julius von Negelein (1872–1932) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Berlin, Marburg, Greifswald, and Königsberg (PhD). He taught at Königsberg before becoming an ordinary professor at Erlangen-Nuremberg in 1920.

Juliusz J. Ossowski (1855–1882) worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and at Königsberg under Adalbert Bezzenberger and Richard von Garbe, earning his PhD.

Jun Fujii (born 1976) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo and held posts at Komazawa University as a lecturer (circa 2010–2013) and as a professor in 2025.
